units.function: Focused environment-diagnostic tests for the local OpenCode adapter, checking an absolute working directory, explicit credential override semantics and classification of an unavailable provider/model probe.
units.dependencyDirection: The server test invokes the adapter package's testEnvironment function with Company and adapter configuration. It reads/mutates the test process environment and filesystem, and the diagnostic implementation executes a configured external command whose stderr is mapped into Paperclip health checks.
units.keyDataModels: Adapter environment request; command/cwd/env configuration; structured health check code/level/hint; aggregate fail/warn status; OPENAI_API_KEY override; vendor ProviderModelNotFoundError probe output.
units.lifecycle: Validate cwd; resolve explicit adapter environment over inherited host environment; invoke a configured probe command; classify known stderr into a model-unavailable warning; return structured checks and aggregate status.
units.testAssessment: All three tests pass. They establish useful stable check codes and the important rule that an explicit empty credential cannot silently fall back to a host secret. However, the suite demonstrates that diagnostics execute an arbitrary configured binary and does not test executable trust, symlink/TOCTOU, process timeout/cancel/output limits, environment allowlisting/redaction, network egress, credential reference resolution, version/capability negotiation or cleanup after hung probes. Model classification depends on vendor/model-specific English stderr.
units.designRationale: Give operators actionable preflight feedback and distinguish bad workspace/credential configuration from a runtime that is installed but lacks the selected model.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs Connector health that is safe for managed-cloud and customer-local execution, reports structured readiness without leaking credentials and does not confuse technical availability with permission to execute work.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the stable health-code and explicit-override semantics. Run active probes only on an authorized execution node under the same sandbox, egress and audit controls as tasks; identify executables by configured Connector package/signature rather than arbitrary control-plane paths; pass opaque secret references resolved locally; allowlist environment keys; cap time/output; redact before transport; report protocol/version/capability/model/data-access readiness separately; distinguish healthy, degraded, unavailable and unauthorized; never let health grant task or data permission. Use structured provider codes with quarantined text-pattern fallbacks.
units.responsibilityConflict: A successful or warning-only probe says nothing about accountable-human assignment, responsibility contract, permission/data scope or approval. Treating a probe-capable adapter as ready could enable code/network execution before the organizational authority chain exists.

units.securityFindings: POSITIVE: missing cwd fails with a stable code; explicit empty credentials do not inherit a host secret; known model unavailability is separated from total failure. CRITICAL active-probe boundary: testEnvironment executes the configured command, so diagnostics are code execution and require authorization, sandbox, timeout, egress and audit controls. HIGH supply-chain gap: no executable identity/signature/version verification is covered. HIGH secret gap: raw environment values remain the configuration shape and no vault reference, allowlist, rotation or redaction behavior is proved. HIGH false-readiness gap: warning status can coexist with inability to run the chosen model and is not capability- or permission-aware. MEDIUM parser fragility: classification depends on English vendor stderr containing provider/model details. MEDIUM filesystem gap: only a missing absolute cwd is tested, not traversal, symlinks, permissions or race changes.
